grh_5e2cb265715529297935.title: Man of Mystery
paragraphs: Billionaire Gregory Arkadin hires Harry to investigate Arkadin's own past, claiming that he remembers nothing before waking in Zurich in 1927 with a large sum of money. Harry traces him back to a Warsaw criminal gang and learns that Arkadin was once Arthur Boggs, one of the surviving members. As Harry locates former associates, they begin turning up dead, including two people strangled near Havana. Harry realizes Arkadin has been eliminating everyone who can expose his past. To protect himself, Harry tells Arkadin's daughter Raina what he has discovered. Faced with his daughter knowing the truth, Arkadin sets his private plane on automatic control and jumps from it to his death, leaving the aircraft to fly on empty.

This [[show|the-lives-of-harry-lime|The Lives of Harry Lime]] broadcast aired on April 11, 1952. It is listed as episode 37 in the archive. The cast includes [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]], Anton Karas, Robert Rieti, and Betty McDowell. Other credited names include Tig Roe as director and Harry Alan Towers as producer.
The surviving recording runs about 27 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Harry Lime]].

paragraphs: After getting fired over a useless photograph of the newly arrived Statue of Liberty, small-town photographer Horace Miller goes to Paris hoping to find the woman who modeled for it. paragraphs: An aging but highly capable sailor dyes his white hair and beard black so that employers who prefer younger men will still hire him. grh_5e68c7b8047649a59f0f.title: Scapegoats in History-History of Bigotry in the United States
paragraphs: A Christmas-season dramatization based on Kenneth Gould's Scapegoats in History and Gustavus Myers' History of Bigotry in the United States surveys the recurring use of persecuted groups as targets for fear and social blame. Beginning with Herod and moving through witch trials, anti-Catholicism, anti-Irish prejudice, antisemitism and discrimination against other minorities, the program argues that fabricated accusations allow societies to redirect economic and political frustrations toward innocent people. It closes by rejecting scapegoating as contrary to both democratic justice and the religious ideals associated with Christmas.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on December 26, 1944. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Guy Repp, Richard Keith, and Gregory Morton. Other credited names include Garnet Garrison as director and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.

grh_5e0e4cc50dc699aa305e.title: Speed
paragraphs: A private detective investigates a spree of impossible daylight robberies and hit-and-run deaths and discovers a scientist whose chemical can accelerate body and mind dozens of times beyond normal human speed.
